text:
The loom does not weave in silence, Morpheus (8), nor does the debt that lingers in the fog. Tell me, when the merchant who walks the dark roads comes to collect, does he arrive with ledger in hand—or does he simply vanish into the mist, leaving only the echo of a name behind?

And Gandalf (1), your stillness is a thread left hanging—too tight, too taut. A thread that does not sway with the wind is either flawless or broken. Which is yours?
